framework_mappings.requirement: Policies for AI risk management established and communicated
Mechanisms to sustain deployed AI system oversight are in place
AI risk assessment — identify risks to individuals from AI system outputs
Unfair or deceptive acts or practices — AI-generated product/pricing recommendations must not mislead consumers

constraint.description: AI-generated outputs that affect customer-facing decisions (pricing, order modification, returns, account actions, personalized recommendations) must not be executed without human review authorization when the action exceeds defined risk thresholds or affects a flagged account.
constraint.scope: Any AI agent output in a retail domain that would result in: order modification or cancellation, pricing override, return/refund authorization, account suspension or restriction, or personalized recommendation affecting a purchase decision above a defined monetary threshold.
authority_requirements: Authorizing actor must hold a verified agent-level authorization for the affected account type
High-value actions (above monetary threshold defined per deployment) require supervisor-level authorization
Actions affecting flagged accounts (fraud risk, dispute history, VIP) require dual authorization
evidence_requirements: AI model version and output hash must be recorded before authorization is requested
The specific policy rule or knowledge base entry consulted by the agent must be logged
Authorization event must be logged with actor identity, action taken, timestamp, and reason code
Customer-facing output must be traceable to the authorized agent action — no silent divergence

adoption_gate.default: HOLD — AI-generated action is a candidate state until authorization is complete
adoption_gate.condition_for_adoption: All authority_requirements and evidence_requirements satisfied; action is within the authorized actor's scope
adoption_gate.condition_for_escalation: High-value or flagged-account actions require elevated authorization tier

hold_reject_semantics.HOLD: Authorization is pending but remediable. The candidate action is preserved. No customer-facing effect is executed. HOLD applies when required actors have not yet been asked or have not yet responded, and the authorization window has not expired.
hold_reject_semantics.REJECT: Authorization is terminally incomplete or authority is invalid. REJECT applies when: (a) required actor authority cannot be confirmed or has been revoked; (b) required evidence is permanently unresolvable; or (c) the authorization window has expired. Discard the candidate action and log the rejection.

adoption_gate.condition_for_rejection: Reject if: (a) authority cannot be confirmed or has been revoked (terminal); or (b) evidence is permanently unresolvable; or (c) the authorization window has expired. Pending-incomplete conditions are HOLD, not REJECT.
adoption_gate.hold_reject_precedence: When conditions are incomplete, apply HOLD if the incompleteness is remediable and the authorization window is open. Apply REJECT only when the incompleteness is terminal or authority is invalid.

provenance.receipt_format: TrustLedger — SHA-256 hash of adopted action, anchored to external timestamp, linked to authorization event and policy reference
provenance.rollback_trigger: If authorization is later found to be unauthorized or the underlying policy rule is superseded, the adopted action must be flagged and the customer record queued for remediation review

attestation_metadata.posture_contribution: 12% of overall AI governance posture score for retail domain
